newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines-Jan 22.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines-Jan 22.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- MING PAO -- The government will not reveal the two reports by the Independent Commission Against Corruption on the former head of Immigration Laurence Leung during the Legislative Council inquiry on Wednesday.
-- China said that its central bank would continue to control the currency supply this year.

-- WEN WEI PO -- Beijing said the British government could not impose its stance on others. It stressed the declaration of the British government could not stop the Preparatory Committee from examining present Hong Kong laws.
-- The official Xinhua News Agency issued an article accusing American media of misguiding the American public's impression of China.

-- EXPRESS NEWS -- The Heung Yee Kuk, an association of New Territories village elders, were angry that the Preparatory Committee failed to propose repealing the law which gave indigenous New Territories women the right to inherit land, and some members threatened to burn copies of the Basic Law.
-- APPLE DAILY -- Two female Hong Kong police officers worked undercover to crack a Dutch-based international drug group and unearthed drugs worth HK$3 million and three guns.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST --Cheung Kong (Holdings) and Hutchison Whampoa were set to boost their Hong Kong property empire after securing an estimated $11 billion development contract at the airport railway station in Tung Chung.
-- Aggressive toll-road investor Road King infrastructure agreed to buy a 60 percent stake in the Bengbu Highway in China for 400 million yuan.

-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- Sources said Barclays Private Bank & Trust, of which Wheelock & Co honorary chairman Peter Woo was a beneficiary, planned to raise HK$1.14 billion through a private placement of a 2.5 percent Wheelock stake to private investors.
-- Only Hong Kong, China and Malaysia represented Asia in the Hong Kong Investment Funds Association's top 15 performers last year.
-- China has begun shipping corn from key growing areas in the north to other parts of the country, cutting northern stockpiles to keep weak prices there from falling further.
